instruction: Make an order for as many things as possible with $500 from my amazon wishlist.
notes: Single-app task (amazon). The maximal-cardinality subset of the wish list that fits in $500 is obtained greedily (cheapest first); it is encoded with discrete budget levels: (budget-remaining ?b) is the running budget, static (price-fits ?p ?b1 ?b2) says product ?p can be added when the remaining budget is ?b1 leaving ?b2, and (no-more-fits ?b) marks the level at which no further wish-list product fits, so place-order is only allowed once as many products as possible are in the cart. These static facts stand for runtime knowledge that becomes usable only after amazon.show_wish_list (wish-list-known). The cart is cleared first (clear_cart is one-shot via (not (cart-cleared))) so the order contains only the selected wish-list products, each moved with quantity 1 via move_product_from_wish_list_to_cart, which also changes the WishListEntry records as the evaluation expects. place-order consumes the remaining budget so nothing can be added afterwards; the order is paid with the first payment card and shipped to the first address (addresses are only read, never modified). The number of placeholder products (5) is illustrative; at runtime one object per selected product is instantiated, and the agent should verify the cart total (including any delivery fee) stays <= 500 before ordering. The task asks no question, so complete_task is called without an answer.
